subproblem.title: The kernels w_j/(c·|w|ⁿ) are locally integrable (Step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, j ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ℝ. Define K(w) := w_j/(c·|w|^{m+1}) on ℝⁿ = Eucl n, where w_j is the j-th coordinate and division by 0 gives 0 (so K(0) = 0, and K ≡ 0 if c = 0). Then K is locally integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure: every point has a neighbourhood on which K is integrable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (j : Fin (m + 1)) (c : ℝ), LocallyIntegrable (fun t : Eucl (m + 1) => t j / (c * ‖t‖ ^ (m + 1)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, which applies it with c = nω_n.

1. Measurability. w ↦ w_j is continuous (it is the continuous linear map EuclideanSpace.proj j), and w ↦ c·|w|^{m+1} is continuous. Hence K is Borel measurable (Measurable.div), so it is a.e. strongly measurable for every measure.

2. Domination. We show |K(w)| ≤ |c|⁻¹·(|w|^m)⁻¹ for every w ∈ ℝⁿ. If c = 0, then K(w) = w_j/0 = 0. If w = 0, then w_j = 0, so K(w) = 0, while the right side is ≥ 0. Otherwise |c| > 0 and |w| > 0, and |w_j| ≤ |w| (PiLp.norm_apply_le). So |K(w)| = |w_j|/(|c|·|w|^{m+1}) ≤ |w|/(|c|·|w|^{m+1}) = |c|⁻¹·(|w|^m)⁻¹.

3. Local integrability. Fix x ∈ ℝⁿ and put R := |x| + 1 > 0. The open ball B_R(0) contains x, so it is a neighbourhood of x. By radial_ball_integral, w ↦ (|w|^m)⁻¹ is integrable on B_R(0), and so is w ↦ |c|⁻¹·(|w|^m)⁻¹. By Steps 1–2 and domination (Integrable.mono'), K is integrable on B_R(0). As x was arbitrary, K is integrable at the neighbourhood filter of every point. That is, K is locally integrable (LocallyIntegrable). ∎
proof_key_steps: K is Borel measurable, and |K(w)| ≤ |c|⁻¹(|w|^m)⁻¹ for all w (cases c = 0 and w = 0; otherwise |w_j| ≤ |w|).
Around x use the ball B_{|x|+1}(0). There (|w|^m)⁻¹ is integrable by radial_ball_integral, so K is integrable by domination.

audit.reason: The arbitrary real constant c is handled correctly, including c = 0 and negative c. Borel measurability and the explicit domination bound, including t = 0, yield integrability on a neighbourhood of every point using radial_ball_integral.
